correctness.rationale: Every finite map splits uniquely into a cycle-set permutation of exact order p and an independently parented rooted forest of exact height h, counted by a label multinomial and layer powers. Mobius inversion yields exact permutation order. Known equivalent-generator structure gives phi(p) generator maps for h=0,1 and exactly one for h>=2. The complete joint and total formulas follow by double counting; the error bound follows from a rigorous product inequality. An independently implemented checker enumerates every transformation on up to six letters, constructs its actual cyclic monoid, verifies all joint cells and fiber sizes, and separately compares exact permutation orders. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established 2023 classification by Elliott–Levine–Mitchell is up to isomorphism and supplies no multiplicities of distinct embedded monoids or stable-rank refinement. The 2014/2017 East–Egri-Nagy–Mitchell work supplies an enumeration algorithm and generator equivalence, including small-degree tables, not the all-degree three-parameter formula. Classical random-mapping work supplies the cycle-plus-forest decomposition, not the quotient by monoid-generator fibers. The new exact joint count and asymptotic are not implied by any inspected statement without an additional full counting argument. Literature priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Embedded monogenic submonoids are a natural exact invariant of full transformation semigroups, distinct from known abstract isomorphism counts. Refining simultaneously by power threshold, eventual period and stable cyclic rank quantifies how abstract cyclic monoids are represented on labeled points. The formula gives all such counts for every degree, distinguishes a structural generator-identification boundary correctly using known algebra, and yields a nontrivial uniform asymptotic n^n with explicit exponential relative bound. It is not a restricted arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the degree-three table.
